facts.statement: Longicrusavis was a ground-dwelling carnivore and wader that was a dominant species in the Jehol Biota ecosystem.
facts.quote: Longicrusavis was a ground dwelling carnivore, a wader, and part of biological family Hongshanornithidae, considered to have been a dominant species in the Jehol Biota

facts.statement: The family name Hongshanornithidae honors the ancient Hongshan culture of China.
facts.quote: The name Hongshanornithidae refers to one of China's oldest recorded cultures in the region, the Hongshan culture.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PKUP V1069 of Longicrusavis was found in the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Longicrusavis is a ground dwelling carnivore known from the holotype specimen PKUP V1069, found from the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The nearly complete skeleton of an adult Longicrusavis preserves carbonized feathers showing visible coloration on the head and forelimbs.
facts.quote: The skeleton is nearly complete and belongs to an adult individual, with carbonized feathers preserved in full plumage with visible colouration around the head and forelimbs.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis possesses hindlimbs that are very long relative to its forelimbs, similar to the related genus Hongshanornis.
facts.quote: Like the closely related genus Hongshanornis, Longicrusavis has hindlimbs that are very long relative to the forelimbs.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis has a more robust rostrum than the closely related genus Hongshanornis.
facts.quote: Longicrusavis has a rostrum that is more robust than that of Hongshanornis.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis exhibits an obvious long, thin, and pointed beak.
facts.quote: Longicrusavis exhibits an obvious long, thin, pointed beak.

facts.statement: Although no teeth are preserved, Longicrusavis likely had teeth in its upper jaw, indicated by alveoli in the premaxilla and maxilla.
facts.quote: Although no teeth are preserved, they were likely present in the upper jaw owing to the presence of alveoli, or tooth sockets, in the premaxilla and maxilla.

facts.statement: The absence of alveoli in the mandible suggests that Longicrusavis was likely edentulous in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: No alveoli are found in the mandible, indicating that it was likely edentulous.

facts.statement: Comparison of tail feathers suggests Longicrusavis represents the oldest known bird form with a long, fan-shaped tail that improved flight.
facts.quote: Comparison of the tail feathers to another similar discovery, both possessing a long fan shaped tail improving flight, suggests these to be the oldest form of bird with this type of tail.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis is scientifically important because detailed evidence of the transition from dinosaurs to birds is rare.
facts.quote: Longicrusavis is important because detailed evidence of transitioning dinosaurs to birds are rare.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis provides evidence of small, specialized birds from the early Cretaceous, dating between 120 and 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Specimen PKUP V1069 also gives us, in conjunction with another palaeontological discovery five years before, evidence a range of small specialised birds from the early Cretaceous, 120-130 million years ago.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis fossils originate from the earlier Yixian and Jiufotang Formation periods within the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: The Jehol Biota never fails to stop giving, and the research to be done on these fossils is virtually endless!" said O'Connor who has determined at least three evolutionary stages to divide history based on the Dabeigou (130ma), Yixian (125ma), and Jiufotang (120ma) Formation periods issuing the Longicrusavis are the earlier Yixian and Jiufotang.

facts.statement: Longicrusavis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Longicrusavis is the family Hongshanornithidae.
The type species of the genus Longicrusavis is Longicrusavis houi.

rejected.statement: Longicrusavis is an extinct genus of basal ornithuromorph bird found exclusively in Dawangzhangzi village, Liaoning Province, China.
rejected.quote: Longicrusavis (meaning "long shin bird" in Latin) is an extinct genus of basal ornithuromorph bird found only at Dawangzhangzi village in Liaoning Province, China.
